responsibility: This module is GCC’s target backend for the MIPS architecture family, covering target-specific code generation, instruction selection, ABI/runtime integration, and processor tuning for MIPS32/MIPS64 systems and their many vendor variants. Its core files (notably mips.h, mips.cc/mips.c, mips.md, predicates.md, and constraints.md) define the target hooks, ISA/ABI rules, register and addressing conventions, calling conventions, prologue/epilogue and PIC handling, builtin expansion, and the master RTL patterns used to lower GCC’s middle-end operations into MIPS instructions. A large set of extension and feature machine descriptions adds support for architectural sub-ISAs and ASEs such as DSP, DSPr2, MSA, paired-single/MIPS-3D, Loongson vector/MMI, microMIPS, fixed-point operations, and synchronization/atomic primitives, while the many per-CPU .md files provide detailed scheduling and latency models for specific MIPS, Loongson, Octeon, Broadcom, and other cores so tuning and instruction scheduling match particular pipelines. The module also contains option and CPU-definition tables for -march/-mtune and related switches, native CPU detection for -march=native, public intrinsic headers for MSA and Loongson extensions, D frontend target hooks, a MIPS-specific frame-header optimization pass, and numerous OS/subtarget configuration headers that adapt the backend to ELF, GNU/Linux, NetBSD, RTEMS, VxWorks, SDE, and other ABI or runtime environments.
